title: Package management
intro: Questions on Linux software distribution and package management. Understanding packages, repositories, and shared libraries is essential for installing software reliably and diagnosing dependency issues.

questions.prompt: What package file format does Debian and Ubuntu use for distributing compiled software?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
`.deb` (Debian package) files are `ar` archives containing:
- `control.tar.gz` — metadata (package name, version, dependencies, maintainer scripts)
- `data.tar.gz` — the actual files to install

Tools:
- `dpkg` — low-level: install/remove/query single `.deb` files
- `apt` — high-level: resolves and downloads dependencies from repositories
- `apt-get` / `apt-cache` — older scriptable interfaces

questions.prompt: What package file format do Red Hat, CentOS, and Fedora use?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
`.rpm` (Red Hat Package Manager) files contain a CPIO archive plus metadata. Tools:

| Tool | Level | Distro |
|---|---|---|
| `rpm` | Low-level (single file) | RHEL/Fedora |
| `yum` | High-level (legacy) | RHEL 7 and earlier |
| `dnf` | High-level (current) | RHEL 8+, Fedora |
| `zypper` | High-level | openSUSE |

`rpm -qi package` shows package info; `rpm -ql package` lists its files.

questions.prompt: What high-level package tool on Debian/Ubuntu resolves dependencies, downloads packages from repositories, and handles upgrades?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
`apt` (Advanced Package Tool) wraps `dpkg` with:
- Dependency resolution (topological sort)
- Repository management
- Download and signature verification

Essential commands:
```bash
apt update           # refresh package index from repos
apt upgrade          # upgrade all installed packages
apt install nginx    # install a package
apt remove nginx     # remove (keep config files)
apt purge nginx      # remove including config files
apt search nginx     # search available packages
```

questions.prompt: What file on Debian/Ubuntu systems lists the APT software repositories — the URLs and suites that apt searches for packages?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
`/etc/apt/sources.list` (and files in `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/`) define package sources:
```
deb https://deb.debian.org/debian bookworm main contrib non-free
deb-src https://deb.debian.org/debian bookworm main
```
- `deb` — binary packages
- `deb-src` — source packages
- `bookworm` — release codename
- `main contrib non-free` — components (by licence)

Run `apt update` after editing to refresh the package index.

questions.prompt: What dpkg command installs a local .deb file directly, without downloading dependencies from a repository?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
`dpkg -i package.deb` installs the package but fails if dependencies are missing. After a failed install, run `apt install -f` to fetch and install the missing dependencies.

```bash
dpkg -i ./myapp_1.0_amd64.deb   # install
dpkg -r myapp                    # remove (keep config)
dpkg -l | grep nginx             # list installed, filter
dpkg -L nginx                    # list files from package
```

questions.prompt: What package manager replaced yum on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and Fedora?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
**dnf** (Dandified YUM) improves on yum with:
- Proper dependency solver (libsolv)
- Better performance and lower memory use
- Module streams (install different versions of a software stack)

```bash
dnf install nginx
dnf update
dnf remove nginx
dnf search nginx
dnf info nginx
```
On RHEL 8+, `yum` is a symlink to `dnf`.

questions.prompt: What is the file extension for Linux shared libraries, loaded at runtime by the dynamic linker?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
`.so` (shared object) files are dynamically linked libraries. They are mapped into process memory on demand. Naming convention: `libname.so.major.minor` (e.g. `libssl.so.3`).

Symlinks chain the names:
```
libopenssl.so → libssl.so.3 → libssl.so.3.0.8
```
Applications link against the unversioned name; the dynamic linker (`ld.so`) resolves the actual `.so` at runtime using the cache built by `ldconfig`.

questions.prompt: What command rebuilds the dynamic linker's shared library cache after a new .so file is installed to a non-standard directory?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
`ldconfig` scans directories listed in `/etc/ld.so.conf` (and `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/`) and rebuilds the cache at `/etc/ld.so.cache`. The dynamic linker reads this cache to locate `.so` files at runtime.

```bash
echo /usr/local/mylib > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/mylib.conf
ldconfig            # rebuild cache
ldconfig -p | grep mylib  # verify
```
Without running `ldconfig`, executables linked against a newly installed library cannot find it.

questions.prompt: What cryptographic mechanism ensures that a downloaded package has not been tampered with and was published by a trusted maintainer?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
**Package signing** uses GPG (PGP) asymmetric cryptography:
1. The repository maintainer signs packages and the repository metadata with their private key
2. The package manager verifies the signature using the public key stored in the trusted keyring

On Debian/Ubuntu:
```bash
apt-key list                    # view trusted keys (deprecated)
ls /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/      # modern key storage
```
If a signature fails, `apt` refuses to install the package — preventing supply-chain attacks.

questions.prompt: What environment variable overrides the default shared library search path for the dynamic linker at runtime?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is searched before the system library cache:
```bash
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/app/lib ./app
```
**Security warning**: The dynamic linker ignores `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for setuid/setgid binaries (a privilege escalation prevention). Never set it permanently in system-wide shell profiles — it can cause unexpected library loading across all processes.

summaryMarkdown:
## Package manager quick reference

| Distro family | Low-level | High-level | Format |
|---|---|---|---|
| Debian/Ubuntu | `dpkg` | `apt` | `.deb` |
| RHEL/Fedora | `rpm` | `dnf` | `.rpm` |
| openSUSE | `rpm` | `zypper` | `.rpm` |
| Arch | `pacman` | `pacman` / `yay` | `.pkg.tar.zst` |
